subject: general
question: If the price of potatoes increases by 10 percent, then by how much percent a user has to cut down on his consumption of potatoes, so that the expenditure on potatoes remains unchanged?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When expenditure is constant, required reduction % = [ R ÷ (100 + R) ] × 100

Here, R = 10% (increase in price)

⇒ Reduction % = [ 10 ÷ (100 + 10) ] × 100

⇒ Reduction % = (10 ÷ 110) × 100 = 100 ÷ 11

⇒ Reduction % = 9.09% ≈ 9.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 9.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in the price of potatoes = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since Expenditure is constant, Consumption is inversely proportional to Price.

⇒ Initial Price = 100%, New Price = 110%

⇒ Price ratio (Old : New) = 100 : 110 = 10 : 11

⇒ Therefore, Consumption ratio (Old : New) = 11 : 10

⇒ Decrease in consumption = 11 − 10 = 1 unit

⇒ Percentage reduction = (Decrease ÷ Old Consumption) × 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = (1 ÷ 11) × 100 = 9.09% ≈ 9.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 9.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed successively by a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by: (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.

Price and Consumption Rule

If the price of a commodity decreases by r%, the increase in consumption so as not to decrease expenditure is [ r ÷ (100 − r) ] × 100.

Base Change Property

If A is R% more than B, then B is [ R ÷ (100 + R) ] × 100% less than A. This same principle applies to price and consumption.
